legend.target_workload: the workload nominated before timing; its whole-model win must repeat before installation
legend.timing_case: the captured input case behind this hypothesis's local kernel timings
legend.timing_workload: the workload behind a region's recorded shipped-kernel speedup
legend.model_ratios: per-workload products of incremental model ratios; diagnostic estimates, not final measurements
legend.p: share of one step this region costs, all copies together, per workload
legend.T_orig_ms: library time for all copies, per workload, from pricing
legend.T_rep_ms: library time for one copy, per workload, from pricing
legend.roofline_ms: estimated ideal cost of one copy from boundary traffic and arithmetic
legend.s_max: optimistic headroom estimate: library time divided by estimated ideal cost
legend.bound: estimated limiting resource: memory, known compute, or launch; custom arithmetic may be unknown
legend.s: speedup shipped: the library's time over the shipped kernel's, both from the kernel's own ship clock
legend.region_ms: the kernel's time for one pass of one copy, from the ship clock
legend.library_ms: the library's time for the same pass, measured beside it
legend.win_ms: library_ms minus region_ms; positive means the kernel is faster
legend.sigma_ms: uncertainty of win_ms; a ship needs a win past three of these
legend.stranded: regions dropped before the search, grouped by reason
legend.steps_per_sample: dependent model steps in one timed sample of the step clock; more than one when a step is too short to bring the GPU clock up on its own
legend.min_win_ms: the least a region win had to save per step on this workload: 1% of the step, at most constants.min_win_ms; the three-sigma rule decides the rest
legend.speedup_vs_plain: under the compiled baseline: the finished model against plain eager MLX, paired in one window at the end of the job; compile's own gain is included, since the model runs compiled
legend.speedup_vs_compiled: under the plain baseline: the finished model (eager plus its kernels) against the untouched model under mx.compile, measured the same way; under 1 means compile alone is faster
legend.plain_win_confirmed: whether that comparison resolved a win past three sigma (compiled_win_confirmed likewise)
legend.plain_loss_confirmed: whether it resolved a loss (compiled_loss_confirmed likewise)
legend.measured_compute_gflops: the plain-matmul rate per dtype clocked in the region's own pricing window; the compute term of its estimated limit divides the region's flops by it
legend.close_rule: why a region's search ended: its budget or the job's is spent, the operator asked to finish, or no discernible headroom (launch-bound, head unmoved by the last two attempts, the last three kernels each within one sigma of the launch floor clocked beside them)
legend.constants.openers_per_region: how many attempts a region's widening round holds at most, each an opener written against the scaffold from a different agent-generated direction; limited by the remaining attempt budget
legend.delivery: how a kernel installs at the region's scope, per workload: direct, graph (the scope compiled with the cut inserted) or replay
legend.library_arm: what the region's clocks ran the library as, per workload: plain ops, or one compiled graph where graph delivery compiles the scope
legend.baseline.clocks_ms.compiled: under library inference: the model with its outermost compilable scopes compiled and empty, the baseline unless the manifest asks for plain
legend.final.delivery: under a plain baseline: the untouched model against the installed scopes compiled with no kernel, and that against the patched model

hypotheses.kind: simdgroup 8x8 matrix tiles from device memory
hypotheses.hypothesis: 16 threadgroups of 4 simdgroups each own a 32x32 output tile; every simdgroup accumulates a 16x16 block as four simdgroup_float8x8 products loaded straight from device memory along K. Replaces the scaffold's 8-threadgroup scalar loop (which loaded each A element per thread 8 times and left most cores idle) with hardware matrix units and 2x more threadgroups; differs from the other openers by using no shared memory and no scalar FMAs.
hypotheses.summary: shipped: whole-model correctness and independent timing confirmation passed

hypotheses.kind: register-blocked 4x4 micro tiles, float4 loads
hypotheses.hypothesis: one thread per 4x4 output block; per k it loads a float4 of B (4 adjacent columns) and 4 A scalars and does 16 FMAs, so 1024 threads spread over 16 threadgroups. Differs from sgmm by using plain ALUs and vector loads, and from the shared-tile design by reading device memory directly.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.kind: threadgroup-memory tiled matmul
hypotheses.hypothesis: 32x32 output tiles with A and B staged through threadgroup memory in K=32 slabs, each thread computing a 4x4 block from shared slabs. Tests whether cutting device reads via reuse in shared memory beats direct-load designs at this tiny size where launch/sync overhead matters.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.kind: one thread per output element, simple wide grid
hypotheses.hypothesis: 64x256 threads, one output each, K loop with float4 loads of the contiguous A row; maximizes threadgroup count (64 groups of 256) with zero register blocking, testing whether pure occupancy wins over reuse for a launch-bound op.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.kind: one simdgroup per threadgroup, 64 small groups
hypotheses.hypothesis: Same 16x16 per-simdgroup simdgroup_float8x8 math as the shipped kernel, but each threadgroup holds a single simdgroup (32 threads), giving 64 threadgroups for N=256 instead of 16. With 10 cores, 16 groups of 128 threads leave cores unevenly loaded; 64 independent small groups should schedule across all cores and shorten the critical path of this latency-bound op.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: whole-model speedup unresolved

hypotheses.kind: software-pipelined K loop with prefetched tiles
hypotheses.hypothesis: Edit the better of shipped/sg_one_per_tg: unroll K by 2 and issue the next step's four simdgroup_loads before the current four multiply_accumulates so device-load latency overlaps matrix math; expects a shorter per-simdgroup critical path.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: whole-model speedup unresolved

hypotheses.kind: 32x32 tile per simdgroup, 4x fewer loads per MMA
hypotheses.hypothesis: Each simdgroup owns a 32x32 tile (16 accumulators): per K step 4 A loads + 4 B loads feed 16 MMAs versus 4 loads for 4 MMAs today, halving load instructions per flop; 16 simdgroups in 16 single-simdgroup threadgroups. Tests whether load count, not group count, bounds the kernel.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.kind: split-K across four simdgroups with threadgroup reduce
hypotheses.hypothesis: The kernel is launch/latency bound (region ~0.007 ms vs 6.7 us launch), so the critical path is the per-simdgroup serial K loop of 16 dependent MMA steps. Each threadgroup of 4 simdgroups owns a 16x16 output tile and each simdgroup accumulates only a quarter of K (4 steps of 8), then the four partial 16x16 tiles are stored to threadgroup memory and summed by the 128 threads. 64 threadgroups (like sg_one_per_tg, the best clock so far) but each simdgroup's dependent chain is 4x shorter. Accumulation order changes (allowed, changing).
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: 8x8 tile per simdgroup, 256 single-simdgroup groups
hypotheses.hypothesis: sg_one_per_tg showed more, smaller threadgroups helped the clock; push further: each 32-thread group computes one 8x8 tile with one accumulator, 256 groups for N=256, 16 K steps of one A load, one B load, one MMA. Tests whether group count beats load amortization at this size; keeps register use minimal to avoid the spill seen in sg_32x32_per_sg.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: whole-model speedup unresolved

hypotheses.kind: 16x8 tile per single-simdgroup group, 128 groups
hypotheses.hypothesis: Split-K lost to reduce overhead (lesson_5), so spend the last attempt between the two best clocks: sg_one_per_tg (64 groups, 16x16 per simdgroup, best clock 0.0065) and sg_8x8_wide (256 groups, 8x8, 0.0077). Each 32-thread group owns a 16x8 tile: per K step 2 A loads + 1 B load feed 2 MMAs (better load amortization than 8x8, half the accumulators of 16x16), giving 128 groups for N=256 to cover all 10 cores several times over.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: whole-model speedup unresolved

hypotheses.kind: one simdgroup per row, fused softmax and PV
hypotheses.hypothesis: 256 threadgroups of 32 threads, one per (batch,row). Each lane holds two scaled scores, simd_max/simd_sum give the row softmax without loops, probabilities go to 64 floats of threadgroup memory, then each lane computes one of the 32 output columns by streaming V's 64 rows. One dispatch, all 10 cores busy, no device scratch; differs from the scaffold's single 128-thread group and from the other openers by having zero redundant softmax work and no simdgroup-matrix hardware.
hypotheses.summary: shipped: whole-model correctness and independent timing confirmation passed

hypotheses.kind: softmax in shared memory then simdgroup_float8x8 P@V
hypotheses.hypothesis: one threadgroup of 256 threads per batch (4 groups): all 64 rows' softmax computed with 8 rows per simdgroup into a 64x64 threadgroup P tile, then the 8 simdgroups each take an 8-row strip and use simdgroup_multiply_accumulate with 8x8 tiles over K=64 against V read directly from device memory. Tests whether MMA throughput beats scalar FMA loops despite fewer groups.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: thread per output element with full softmax recompute
hypotheses.hypothesis: 8192 threads, each owning one output element: it scans its row's 64 scores for max, then accumulates exp(x-max)*V[k,col] and the sum in one pass, dividing at the end. No barriers, no threadgroup memory, 32x redundant exp work but at 16K scores total that is tiny; tests whether pure independence beats sync-based designs at this launch-bound size.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: two dispatches: softmax stage then matmul stage
hypotheses.hypothesis: stage 1 writes normalized probabilities [4,64,64] with one simdgroup per row; stage 2 is a plain thread-per-output matmul reading them. Two launches instead of one but each is simple and wide; tests whether the fused kernels lose to splitting the two phases at this size, and gives a parent for the matmul stage alone.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.kind: registers only: broadcast P via simd_shuffle, no threadgroup memory or barrier
hypotheses.hypothesis: Keep the shipped one-simdgroup-per-row layout but drop the threadgroup P array and its barrier: each lane keeps its two unnormalized exp values in registers and the PV loop pulls p[k] with simd_broadcast, normalizing acc by 1/sum once at the end instead of 64 divides. Removes threadgroup memory allocation and one barrier per group, which at a launch-bound 0.007 ms size may shave latency per group.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: 64-thread groups covering two rows, halving group count
hypotheses.hypothesis: Same per-simdgroup math as the shipped kernel but 128 groups of 64 threads (two simdgroups, one row each) so the V slice for the batch is more likely shared in L1 across the two rows and scheduler overhead per group halves; tests whether 256 tiny groups is more than the 10 cores want.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: whole-model speedup unresolved

hypotheses.kind: lanes own 4 V columns via float4 loads, 8 lanes per row, 4 rows per simdgroup
hypotheses.hypothesis: Each simdgroup handles 4 rows: 8 lanes per row, each lane holds 8 scores, row softmax via shuffle-xor reductions over 8 lanes, and the PV loop loads V rows as float4 (4 columns per lane) so V traffic per row is 16 float4 loads instead of 64 scalar loads per lane; 64 groups of 32 threads. Tests wider per-lane vector loads against the scalar shipped loop.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: whole-model speedup unresolved

hypotheses.kind: multiply by constant scale, normalize once after PV, unrolled float4 P reads
hypotheses.hypothesis: Keep the shipped one-simdgroup-per-row layout but shave scalar work: scores are multiplied by the constant 1/sqrt(32) instead of divided, the unnormalized exps go to threadgroup memory and the 1/sum multiply is applied once to the accumulator after PV (2 divides per lane become 1 multiply), and the 64-step PV loop reads P as float4 with 4-way unroll so it issues fewer threadgroup loads and address computations. Tests whether the ~3.3 us above floor is partly per-thread instruction latency rather than launch cost.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: whole-model speedup unresolved

hypotheses.kind: 256-thread groups own 8 rows and stage the batch V slice in threadgroup memory
hypotheses.hypothesis: 32 groups of 256 threads (8 simdgroups, one row each); the group cooperatively loads its batch's 8 KB V slice into threadgroup memory as float4 (2 per thread) before the PV loop so the 8 rows read V from shared memory instead of each hitting L1 separately; between sgmatrix_pv's 4 groups and the shipped 256 groups, tests whether V sharing at a mid group count pays.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: whole-model speedup unresolved

hypotheses.kind: 16 lanes per row, each lane owns two adjacent V columns via float2
hypotheses.hypothesis: Each simdgroup handles 2 rows with 16 lanes per row: each lane holds 4 scores, reductions take 4 shuffle steps instead of 5, and the PV loop loads float2 (2 columns) per lane so 128 groups of 32 threads each finish two rows; a middle point between the shipped scalar loop and the float4/8-lane layout that lost.

hypotheses.kind: one thread per interleaved pair
hypotheses.hypothesis: The scaffold launches a single 128-thread threadgroup that loops over all 8192 outputs, so one core does all the work. Launch one thread per (in0,in1) element pair across the whole grid: each thread does two loads and two adjacent stores, spreading the copy over every core. Expected to approach the streaming floor since the op is pure data movement.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: float4 vectorized loads and stores
hypotheses.hypothesis: Each thread loads a float4 from in0 and a float4 from in1 (16 contiguous elements along the last axis are 4-aligned), interleaves in registers, and writes two float4 vectors to out0. Fewer threads and wider memory transactions than the pair-per-thread design; tests whether transaction width matters at this tiny size.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: one thread per output element with parity select
hypotheses.hypothesis: Launch 2*N threads, one per output element; thread i selects in0 or in1 by parity and issues a single store. Maximally simple thread body, twice the thread count; contrasts with the pair design by trading store width for occupancy.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: threadgroup-memory staged tile
hypotheses.hypothesis: Each 128-thread threadgroup stages 128 elements of in0 and in1 into threadgroup memory with fully coalesced loads, then each thread writes two consecutive outputs read from shared memory. Tests whether decoupling load and store patterns helps versus direct register interleave.

hypotheses.kind: single float2 store per pair
hypotheses.hypothesis: One thread per (in0,in1) pair, but the interleaved pair is written as one 8-byte float2 store instead of two scalar stores; halves store instruction count versus pair_per_thread while keeping the fully coalesced scalar loads. Tests whether store instruction count, not transaction width, moves this launch-bound copy.

hypotheses.kind: many pairs per thread, tiny grid
hypotheses.hypothesis: Each thread handles a whole 16-element row of both inputs via four float4 loads each and writes eight float4 stores; grid shrinks to 256 threads across few threadgroups, testing whether fewer, fatter threads shave per-threadgroup scheduling overhead on this 32KB launch-bound region.

hypotheses.kind: 64-thread threadgroups with float2 store
hypotheses.hypothesis: Same body as float2_store but 64-thread threadgroups so the grid spans more threadgroups across all 10 cores; tests threadgroup-count sensitivity at this tiny size.

hypotheses.kind: two pairs per thread as one float4 store, 32-thread simdgroup-sized groups
hypotheses.hypothesis: Each thread loads two consecutive elements from in0 and in1 (float2 loads, 8-byte aligned since the last axis is 16 wide) and writes one 16-byte float4 (a0,b0,a1,b1). Half the threads of float2_store with the same total store bytes per thread doubled, and 32-thread threadgroups so every threadgroup is exactly one simdgroup, spreading 128 small groups across the 10 cores. Tests whether the smallest scheduling unit plus 16-byte stores lowers the fixed per-dispatch cost below the ~5us floor.
